children: Oil markets are unlikely to rebalance until mid-2027, HSBC analyst Kim Fustier says in a note. She says HSBC's base case is for a fragile U.S.-Iran understanding to emerge but that would remain prone to recurring breakdowns and uncertainty over security and insurance. She expects flows through the Strait of Hormuz to rise from 6 million barrels/day currently to 8 million by year-end and 9.5 million by mid-2027, well below pre-conflict levels of 19 million-20 million. Against this tighter outlook, HSBC raises its 2026 Brent crude forecast to $90 from $80 per barrel. Under a 'stalemate' scenario where diplomacy fails and flows remain constrained, inventories could hit operational lows, potentially driving Brent to around $120 a barrel. Front-month Brent futures are down 0.3% at $100.95 a barrel. (venkat.pr@wsj.com)
